## 2

I don't agree, and here's where we'd actually disagree. The flat-earth claim has to explain away an enormous amount of ordinary evidence: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, the way the available constellations change as you travel north or south, time zones, the fact that you can fly a continuous route around the world, the roughly 24-hour lag of sunlight across longitudes. Those all fall out naturally from a globe and need elaborate patches on a flat model.

On the faked photos: that requires not just NASA but every other space agency (including rivals like Roscosmos and CNSA, who'd love to catch each other lying), plus thousands of amateurs who track satellites with backyard gear, all coordinating a lie for decades without a leak. What specifically convinced you? I'd rather dig into the actual reason than just trade claims.

## 3

Okay, so sunlight looks white, but it's actually all the colors mixed together. You can split them back out with a prism, or a rainbow.

Now, light travels in waves, and the different colors have different wave sizes. Blue and violet are the short, tight ones; red is the long, stretched-out one.

Here's the key part. Our air is full of tiny molecules, way too small to see. When sunlight hits them, the short wavelengths (blue) get knocked off course and scattered all over the sky far more than the long ones. So when you look up at any random patch of sky, you're seeing all that blue light bouncing around and coming at you from every direction.

One good follow-up question: if blue and violet both scatter, why isn't the sky violet? Partly because the sun sends out less violet to begin with, and partly because your eyes are more sensitive to blue. So blue wins.

And at sunset the light has to travel through much more air to reach you, so the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, leaving the reds and oranges. Same physics, different angle.

## 4

雨在午夜悄悄下了起来，起初只是细碎的声响，后来渐渐密了，敲在屋檐和窗玻璃上，连成一片。街灯把雨丝照成一条条斜斜的银线，路面上积了浅浅的水洼，倒映着忽明忽暗的光。偶尔有车驶过，轮胎碾过水面，溅起一道白沫，又很快归于平静。远处的楼影模糊在雨雾里，只剩几扇还亮着的窗。我靠在窗边，听着雨声，手里的茶慢慢凉了，心里却觉得格外安稳，仿佛整座城市都被这场雨温柔地盖住了。
